title: FancyZones exclude by pressing shift during drag no longer working
author: Chrisch-Tea
summary: A recent FancyZones input-hook change appears to have regressed zone exclusion when Shift is pressed after a drag begins.

status.label: Regression design ready
status.detail: The version-bounded reproduction and history point to the changed Shift-during-drag path.

next_action.label: Design and test Shift state fix
next_action.reason: Validate key state propagation and remove the timing or stale-state gap.

judgment.rationale: The reproduction is precise, the prior release worked, and a recent change modified the exact path.
evidence: On 0.101.2362, mid-drag Shift no longer excludes the window.
The issue was absent in the previous build.
Commit d68980a81b in #49985 changed OnKeyDown to set Shift while swallowing it.
judgment.recommended_action: Continue focused regression design and UI tests; keep design_in_progress until the exact state transition is proven.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones no longer honors exclusion when Shift is introduced mid-drag, while pre-held Shift remains correct.
known_information: Hold Shift to activate zones is disabled, so Shift should suppress zoning.
The test uses Notepad on Windows 11 build 26200.9106.
Pre-held Shift works; mid-drag Shift fails.
No duplicate, assignee, or linked fix exists.
inferences: The explicit SetShiftState call may not synchronize with the final MoveSize update, or release state may be inconsistent.
The regression likely ties to the August 21 change in this path.
issue_context.analysis: The report already provides the decision-changing timing distinction. Code reproduction and tests are next, not a generic diagnostic request.
initial_investigation: DraggingState.cpp computes zoning from Shift and drag mode.
OnKeyboardInput updates Shift from raw input.
OnKeyDown now calls SetShiftState(true) before swallowing bare Shift during WindowMouseSnap.
#49985 introduced the change on 2026-08-21; current main retains it.
